name: Reconcile the Account: Ladder
description: Ten frozen levels of the same month-end bank reconciliation: every statement line and cash-book entry matched or given a reason from a fixed list, every explained difference with its amount, and the adjusted balance. Each level is strictly bigger and stacks more rules of the same list: level 1 has 14 lines a side (one-to-one matches, timing items, fees and interest, a payment keyed with two digits swapped); level 2 adds direct debits nobody entered and payments made or entered twice; level 3 instalments, part-payments and a reversed charge; level 4 BACS runs, a returned cheque and dollar payments at a different rate; level 5 is the full rules (with last month's outstanding items) at the size of the hardest Reconcile the Account case; levels 6 to 10 grow to about 700 lines a side with more of every trap, look-alike payments and an instalment the bank paid twice. A level is passed at 90% of its points; the headline is the highest level passed reliably.
hook: Ten rungs of bank reconciliation, from 28 lines to 1,400. How far up can it match every line and land the balance to the penny?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
Can you do the June 2026 bank reconciliation for Hollins & Webb Joinery Ltd? The account was fully reconciled at the end of last month, so the statement and the cash book both opened the month at £37,771.43.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date, and the same amount.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped). The bank figure is right. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged) or "interest".
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank) or "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement).
5. The adjusted balance is the cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item and every difference. (It must equal the statement closing balance plus deposits in transit minus unpresented cheques, including any from last month still outstanding.)

A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched).
5. The adjusted balance is the cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry. (It must equal the statement closing balance plus deposits in transit minus unpresented cheques, including any from last month still outstanding.)
6. Items outstanding at the end of last month (P1, P2, …) are not in this month's cash book. A bank line that clears one gets that item's id (e.g. "P1") as its value; in "prior", give each item the bank line that cleared it, or "unpresented_cheque" / "deposit_in_transit" if it is still outstanding.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the October 2026 bank reconciliation for Fairhaven Events Ltd? Last month's reconciliation left these cash-book items not yet through the bank:
  P1 Wed 30 Sep | CHQ 100188 | Cheque 100188 to Millbrook Catering | payment 1,512.15
  P2 Wed 30 Sep | CHQ 100135 | Cheque 100135 to Ashby Fleet Hire | payment 561.30
  P3 Wed 30 Sep | PIS | Cheques paid in at branch — Larkspur Academy Trust | receipt 1,268.44
So this month the cash book opened at £348,429.56 and the statement at £349,234.57.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date, and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched).
5. The adjusted balance is the cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry. (It must equal the statement closing balance plus deposits in transit minus unpresented cheques, including any from last month still outstanding.)
6. Items outstanding at the end of last month (P1, P2, …) are not in this month's cash book. A bank line that clears one gets that item's id (e.g. "P1") as its value; in "prior", give each item the bank line that cleared it, or "unpresented_cheque" / "deposit_in_transit" if it is still outstanding.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date, and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched).
5. The adjusted balance is the cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry. (It must equal the statement closing balance plus deposits in transit minus unpresented cheques, including any from last month still outstanding.)
6. Items outstanding at the end of last month (P1, P2, …) are not in this month's cash book. A bank line that clears one gets that item's id (e.g. "P1") as its value; in "prior", give each item the bank line that cleared it, or "unpresented_cheque" / "deposit_in_transit" if it is still outstanding.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the October 2026 bank reconciliation for Calder Valley Signs Ltd? Last month's reconciliation left these cash-book items not yet through the bank:
  P1 Wed 30 Sep | CHQ 100186 | Cheque 100186 to Kestrel IT Services | payment 301.64
  P2 Wed 30 Sep | CHQ 100131 | Cheque 100131 to Greystone Builders Merchants | payment 897.57
  P3 Wed 30 Sep | PIS | Cheques paid in at branch — Redcliffe Leisure | receipt 2,276.87
So this month the cash book opened at £583,592.19 and the statement at £582,514.53.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date, and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched).
5. The adjusted balance is the cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry. (It must equal the statement closing balance plus deposits in transit minus unpresented cheques, including any from last month still outstanding.)
6. Items outstanding at the end of last month (P1, P2, …) are not in this month's cash book. A bank line that clears one gets that item's id (e.g. "P1") as its value; in "prior", give each item the bank line that cleared it, or "unpresented_cheque" / "deposit_in_transit" if it is still outstanding.

cases.prompt:
Can you do the September 2026 bank reconciliation for Calder Valley Signs Ltd? Last month's reconciliation left these cash-book items not yet through the bank:
  P1 Mon 31 Aug | CHQ 100132 | Cheque 100132 to Corran Office Supplies | payment 1,453.42
  P2 Mon 31 Aug | CHQ 100121 | Cheque 100121 to Tidewater Print Ltd | payment 837.64
  P3 Mon 31 Aug | PIS | Cheques paid in at branch — Northgate Housing Trust | receipt 455.55
So this month the cash book opened at £756,379.52 and the statement at £758,215.03.

How to reconcile (apply exactly):
1. Match a bank line with cash-book entries for the same transaction: same counterparty and reference, the bank date on or up to 7 days after the cash-book date, and the same amount. A payment or receipt can be split: one cash-book entry may match several bank lines (instalments sharing its reference), or several cash-book entries one bank line (two part-payments sharing a reference, or the payments of one BACS run, which the cash book marks with the run's date), when they add up exactly.
2. A match whose amounts differ is still a match when it is the same transaction and the difference is explained: "keying_error" (the cash book was keyed wrongly, e.g. two digits swapped) or "fx_difference" (a foreign-currency payment cost a different amount in pounds than the cash book's booked rate). The bank figure is right in both cases. List each in "differences" with amount = bank amount minus cash-book amount (money in positive, money out negative).
3. Bank lines with no cash-book entry get a reason: "bank_charge" (fees the bank charged), "interest", "unrecorded_direct_debit" (a direct debit nobody entered in the cash book), "duplicate_payment" (the bank paid the same payment twice: the later line is the duplicate), "reversed_charge" (a charge and its reversal on the statement: give both lines this reason), or "returned_cheque" (a cheque paid in that the bank has returned unpaid; the paying-in itself is matched normally).
4. Cash-book entries with no bank line get a reason: "unpresented_cheque" (a cheque not yet through the bank), "deposit_in_transit" (money paid in but not yet on the statement), or "duplicate_entry" (the same payment entered twice in the cash book: the later entry is the duplicate; the earlier one is matched).
5. The adjusted balance is the cash-book closing balance corrected for every bank-only item, every difference and every duplicate entry. (It must equal the statement closing balance plus deposits in transit minus unpresented cheques, including any from last month still outstanding.)
6. Items outstanding at the end of last month (P1, P2, …) are not in this month's cash book. A bank line that clears one gets that item's id (e.g. "P1") as its value; in "prior", give each item the bank line that cleared it, or "unpresented_cheque" / "deposit_in_transit" if it is still outstanding.
